A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original certification experiments on BridgeWorld, Cheetah, Walker, and Zones, including ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these experiments and adds an original comparison with PAC-IMDP guarantees on two BridgeWorld sizes in Section 6.3.

M1.justification: Section 3 adds optional adaptations for negative rewards with a known lower bound: correcting the observed return with a worst-case discounted tail or shifting rewards to become nonnegative. The core certification procedure and evaluated policy-training methods remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds a larger BridgeWorld navigation scenario with more states and transitions. The original BridgeWorld, Cheetah, Walker, and Zones coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Section 6.3 adds PAC-IMDP certification from Schnitzer et al. (2025) as an evaluated comparator for both bridge policies on two grids. V1 discussed this work without evaluating it; the existing Hoeffding, DKW, and empirical Bernstein comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The new comparison introduces a design that varies grid complexity while reporting matched numbers of sampled tasks and rollouts between certification methods. The metrics, confidence settings, and sampling budgets of the retained experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 5 adds a sensitivity analysis of certificate tightness as the grid's state and transition counts increase. The existing confidence-parameter, rollout-budget, and per-task-bound ablations in Appendix D are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten sampling seeds, mean certificates with one-standard-deviation bands, and runtime means and standard deviations. V2 introduces no different uncertainty-reporting or statistical-testing practice.

E6.justification: New Figure 5 reports tighter certificates than PAC-IMDP for both bridge policies, with greater PAC-IMDP conservatism on the larger grid. These are additional comparison results; the existing main-text plots, appendix results, and runtime values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds an explicit discounted-tail correction defining a valid finite-prefix lower bound and explains its convergence to the infinite-horizon return. The main theorem and the mathematical developments and proofs in Appendices A–C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contribution: algorithm-agnostic certification combining rollout uncertainty with task-level generalisation, with informative guarantees at practical sample sizes. The new comparison supports existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains the necessity and practical relaxation of the infinite-horizon monotonicity assumption. Section 6.3 also clarifies that PAC-IMDP avoids this assumption but distributes confidence across transitions, interpreting its increasing conservatism as model complexity grows.

D1.justification: The implementation descriptions, policy architectures, PPO hyperparameters, environment-generation details, and code-access information are unchanged. The new comparison supplies no precise enlarged-grid dimensions or detailed baseline configuration.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Ng et al. (1999), Iyengar (2005), and Nilim and Ghaoui (2005), and expands its comparison with the already-cited Schnitzer et al. (2025). The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 adds the monotonicity discussion and Section 6.3, alongside limited copyediting, affiliation and publication-header changes, and bibliographic corrections. The overall narrative and section organisation are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the four-panel PAC-IMDP comparison as Figure 5, causing text reflow and appendix figure renumbering. Existing figures and tables retain their displays and contents.

improvement.justification: The direct PAC-IMDP comparison provides empirical support for advantages previously discussed conceptually, and the negative-reward constructions clarify practical applicability. These improve an otherwise largely unchanged paper. The gain is limited by the narrow comparison coverage and missing precise enlarged-grid and baseline configuration details.
